paper_title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
core_problem: Large language models are increasingly used to interact with external environments e.g., games, compilers, APIs as goal-driven agents, but it remains challenging for these language agents to quickly and efficiently learn from trial-and-error as traditional reinforcement learning methods require extensive training samples and expensive model fine-tuning.
methodology_summary: Reflexion is a framework to reinforce language agents not by updating weights but through linguistic feedback. Agents verbally reflect on task feedback signals and maintain their own reflective text in an episodic memory buffer to induce better decision-making in subsequent trials. The framework is flexible enough to incorporate various types scalar values or free-form language and sources external or internally simulated of feedback signals.
empirical_results: Reflexion obtains significant improvements over a baseline agent across diverse tasks including sequential decision-making, coding and language reasoning. On the HumanEval coding benchmark Reflexion achieves 91% pass@1 accuracy, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art GPT-4 that achieves 80%.
explicit_limitations: No explicit limitations are provided in the given context.
